item.title: Molecular pendulum shuttles protons to enable rapid hydrogen production in enzymes
item.description: Nearly all metabolic processes require protons—positively charged hydrogen atoms. Although these are abundant in the cellular fluid, the biocatalysts involved depend on mechanisms for efficiently capturing protons and transporting them to the site where catalysis occurs. Enzymes from microorganisms can produce hydrogen (H₂) by combining electrons with protons. These so-called hydrogenases are so efficient that one biocatalyst can capture nearly 10,000 protons per second. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: '24/7 unmanned synthesis platform' uses robots and light to produce drug candidates
item.description: Even when AI designs molecules with potential as medicines, drug development can be delayed if the process of producing them is slow. The technology is expected to help secure a wider range of drug candidate compounds by reducing the burden of repetitive experiments. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: X-rays reveal surprisingly long-lived spin waves in copper oxide
item.description: Today's computer technology, based on silicon chips, is slowly reaching its physical limits. Components cannot be miniaturized indefinitely, and clock speeds cannot be increased indefinitely. At the same time, huge AI data centers are being built in many places, and these consume an immense amount of electricity. This is why scientists around the world are searching for novel materials that can replace or complement silicon technology and consume significantly less electricity. Fuente: Phys.org.
